_comment: NO NULL ORG (owner ruling 2026-08-21, db-rules FEATURE.md §2/§6e). Seeded from LIVE, not from zero — the gate's job is preventing growth, not forcing an instant cleanup, and it must never be able to block a release on the legacy backlog. `null_org_rows_total` may only go DOWN; `nullable_org_columns` may only SHRINK. Raising either is an Arman decision; agents shrink them with --update-baseline.

known_null_org_writers.reason: The system error queue still appends NULL-org rows continuously (newest one minutes old at seeding). All 8,495 of its NULL-org rows also have user_id NULL: these are genuinely system-context errors, so under the ruling they belong to the SYSTEM ORG, not to a personal org. Fixing the capture path is real work on a live high-volume error lane and is chipped separately; until then this table's growth is reported RED but does not block. It may never be an excuse for the pattern — remove this entry when the capture path stamps the system org.

The secret-access audit trail still appends NULL-org rows continuously (newest one minutes old at seeding). It carries user_id, so the personal-org backstop can resolve every row and the fix is mechanical; it is chipped separately. Until then its growth is reported RED but does not block. Remove this entry when the audit writer stamps the org.

The studio recording-chunk append path was minting NULL-org rows seconds before this gate was seeded (a live recording session). Chunks are components of a recording session that already carries an org, so the fix is platform.inherit_org_from_parent on the session FK rather than a personal-org guess; chipped separately. Until then its growth is reported RED but does not block. Remove this entry when the chunk writer inherits the session's org.
